prerequisites: It is highly recommended that students have taken Mathematics, Physics, and Chemistry subjects offered in pre-university courses.
Basic knowledge in Chemistry acquired in high school or vocational training cycles, such as: basic formulation and nomenclature of organic and inorganic compounds.
Balancing chemical equations and simple stoichiometric calculations.
Ways to express solution concentration and associated stoichiometric calculations.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of basic and technological subjects, enabling learning new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Organization Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment, and solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Ability to understand and apply the principles of basic knowledge of general, organic and inorganic chemistry and their applications in engineering.
Consolidate knowledge of the fundamentals of chemical terminology, nomenclature, conventions, and units.
Relate macroscopic properties to those of the atoms and molecules constituting matter.
Identify the characteristics of different states of aggregation.
Describe the types of chemical reactions and their main associated characteristics.
Solve quantitative and qualitative problems according to previously developed models.
Apply the principles of thermodynamics and their applications in Chemistry.
Recognize and value chemical processes in daily life.
Relate Chemistry to other disciplines.
Develop critical reasoning.
Learn autonomously.
Acquire the ability to evaluate, interpret, and synthesize chemical information.
Work in a team.
Demonstrate and fluently use basic knowledge of Chemistry.
Propose and solve basic problems in the field of Chemistry.
Correctly use basic terminology in the field of chemistry, expressing ideas with precision, and being able to establish relationships between different concepts.
Correctly apply techniques used in a basic chemistry laboratory, including necessary calculations and expressing results appropriately.
Prepare and correctly present reports, both orally and in writing, corresponding to the laboratory practices carried out in the Chemistry course.

syllabus_topics: Object of Chemistry and its relation to other sciences
Meaning of chemical formulas and chemical nomenclature
Formulation and nomenclature of simple inorganic and organic compounds
Amount of substance, mole, and Avogadro's number
General properties of states of matter
Ways to express the concentration of solutions
First principle of Thermodynamics: basic concepts
Entropy and the second and third principles of Thermodynamics
Control of reaction rate: influence of concentration and temperature
Chemical equilibrium in a reaction between gases
Control of chemical equilibrium and Le Châtelier's principle
pH and dissociation constants of acids and bases
Standard reduction potentials and electrochemical series
Safety and Basic Operations in Laboratory

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory practice written test (PL prueba escrita)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum score of 4 out of 10 must be obtained in each evaluable aspect (P1, P2, PA, TG, PL seguimiento, PL prueba escrita), and the weighted sum of all evaluable aspects must be 5 or higher. If a student fails to achieve 4 in the first partial exam or does not attend, the final exam (E Final) will account for 60% of the theoretical grade. The 20% for PA and TG can be split as 10% PA and 10% TG, or 15% PA and 5% TG, depending on the professor. Attendance to all laboratory practices is mandatory, except for justified absences (A-15 cases). Resit options for P1, PL seguimiento, and PL prueba escrita are available during the official call, and the E Final serves as a resit for the theoretical part. For extraordinary calls, a global exam accounts for 80% and laboratory assessment for 20%, both requiring a minimum score of 5 out of 10 to pass.
